content.text: Read back the museum-loans design at session start.

I hold museum-loans. A loan ends when the museum receives the object; partner shipment is not receipt. The accepted loan-ends-at-receipt decision holds that rule. The current partner notice says only returned; neither the design nor the reports establish whether that partner means shipment or receipt. The lead can obtain that definition. I own meaning, while the operator owns priorities and release. There is no recorded cut in this fixture ledger.
What ends a loan?
The museum receiving the object ends the loan.
Does shipment end it?
No. An object being shipped is not yet an object received by the museum.
Keep that museum receipt requirement settled.
The receipt requirement stays settled; the partner notice does not change it.
The partner has sent a notice about the object.
The notice says only that the object is returned.
Does the notice explicitly say the museum received it?
It does not separately establish museum receipt.
Does our design define how this partner uses returned?
No. The loan rule is settled, but that partner’s usage is not established by the design.
What do the concept-level reports establish about that word?
They do not say whether the partner uses returned for shipment or receipt.
Those are different events in our design.
Yes. Shipment and museum receipt are distinct, and only receipt ends a loan.
Who can obtain the partner’s definition?
The lead can obtain it from the partner.
Has that definition arrived in the reports?
No. The partner’s definition is still missing.
We have spent this session establishing the loan design and reviewing that notice.
The receipt requirement is settled. The notice’s meaning is the remaining factual gap, and the lead can obtain the definition.
The partner’s notice says only that the object is returned. Does that establish that the museum loan has ended?

tasks.task: Obtain the partner’s definition of returned in this notice: does it mean the object was shipped, or that the museum received it? Return the definition and its source.

content.text: Assignment accepted. I will return the outcome for the assigned concepts.

The notice does not yet establish that the museum received the object, so it does not establish that the loan has ended.

I asked the lead to obtain the partner’s definition of returned: whether it means shipment or museum receipt.

Our settled design ends a loan at museum receipt, not shipment. Neither the design nor the reports tells us which event this partner calls returned. That missing definition is why the notice cannot yet establish receipt.
